item.title: 3 takeaways from Iowa State football's loss at UCF | Hines
item.description: Iowa State football's first season under coach Jimmy Rogers will resoundingly land on the "Success" side of the ledger, given all the Cyclones have accomplished with all that was against them. A season that many feared could turn into a nightmare has been a pleasant surprise. But that doesn't mean it's been free of frustrations or its own disappointments. Riding high after its best performance of the season and needing a single win to clinch bowl eligibility, the Cyclones were, well, they stunk at UCF in a 48-17 loss on Nov. 20. Your opinion on where it lands in the hierarchy of poor performances in the six losses suffered by Iowa State (5-6, 3-5 Big 12) will vary, but it gets consideration for the top spot. UCF (6-5, 4-4) came into the game looking very evenly matched with the Cyclones, but the Knights took advantage of four Iowa State turnovers and their own explosive plays to turn this into a rout early in the second half. After last week's 41-13 home win against Cincinnati, it appeared as though Iowa State was playing its best football of the year and poised to potentially win back-to-back games for the first time this season. Instead, the offense couldn't protect or move the ball, and the defense, while put in tough positions with the turnovers, wasn't up to the task of bottling up a middling Big 12 offense. The nation's leading rusher, Aiden Flora, was sensational again with 171 yards rushing to go over 1,500 for the season for the Cyclones, but it wasn't near enough to overcome the turnovers and a passing attack that didn't eclipse 100 yards until the final minutes of the fourth quarter. Iowa State can still get bowl-eligible. The Cyclones can finish the season on a high note. But they'll have to bounce back from what happened in the Bounce House to do it. Home/road splits I'm not saying if Iowa State played 12 home games this season that the Cyclones would be a top-four seed in the College Football Playoff, but I'm not ruling it out, either? I'm not saying if Iowa State played 12 road games this season that the Cyclones would be winless, but I'm not ruling it out, either? This outing in Orlando is just another chapter in the yawning expanse between the quality of play from Iowa State at home versus on the road. At home, the Cyclones are dangerous. On the road, the Cyclones are a calamity. I'm not sure if there's a simple explanation for it beyond the usual tangible and intangible differences between playing in your own stadium versus some else's, but the results certainly speak for themselves. Iowa State scored an average of 38.5 points while giving up 33.8 at home during Big 12 play. On the road, the Cyclones are scoring 15.3 points while surrendering 38.2. With still one final home game against a pretty hapless Kansas State team, the Cyclones should be able to get bowl-eligible by going winless on the road, but that's a streak that will follow them into the offseason and 2027. item.title: Field Yates has serious questions about Rams GM Les Snead’s draft choices amid frustrating season
item.description: Kirby Lee-Imagn Images Field Yates has serious questions about Rams GM Les Snead’s draft choices amid frustrating season appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Los Angeles Rams may be riding a four-game winning streak. However, their 2026 offseason blueprint is facing uncomfortable questions . That’s particularly true regarding general manager Les Snead ’s draft decisions. ESPN NFL analyst Field Yates recently highlighted an interesting disconnect. It’s between Los Angeles’ aggressive win-now approach in free agency and the lack of immediate contributions from its draft class. The Rams have recorded the third-fewest rookie snaps in the NFL this season. They are ahead of only the Broncos and Seahawks. That has raised questions about whether their draft investments are delivering enough value. Snead’s decision to select quarterback Ty Simpson 13th overall as Matthew Stafford’s eventual successor instead of immediate-impact prospects such as Kenyon Sadiq or Makai Lemon has become a focal point of the discussion . "If this season doesn't result in meaningful winning, people are going to question this past draft." @FieldYates breaks down the issues facing the Rams and what's at stake moving forward ✍️ pic.twitter.com/dGMttiZo5v Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) — NFL on ESPN (@ESPNNFL) November 20, 2026 “Fairly or unfairly, their decision in April to draft the quarterback in Ty Simpson 13th overall and basically say we’re punting on our first-round pick for this year is going to be reviewed in some ways as a results-based pick, not a process-based pick,” Yates explained. The scrutiny is particularly significant given the Rams’ decision to prioritize an all-in push while postponing extensions for key homegrown talents. Those include Puka Nacua, Byron Young, and Kobie Turner. With Nacua and Davante Adams currently sidelined , Los Angeles’ limited contributions from its draft class have become even more noticeable. Yates warned that the stakes could rise considerably if the Rams fail to translate their recent momentum into meaningful postseason success. Los Angeles currently sits at 6-4 entering its Week 11 bye. That’s after overcoming a rough 2-4 start and injuries to key receivers. The turnaround has been impressive, but Snead’s draft strategy may ultimately be judged by how far this team goes. item.description: Kaleena Smith #11 of Ontario Christian High School poses for a portrait at The Knights Center on November 9, 2026 in Ontario, California. ONTARIO, Calif -- No. 1 Kaleena Smith passes 3,000 points in Ontario Christians Homer Opener. With no time to waste, Kaleena Smith drains a three pointer to hit 3,000 career points in the first play of the game. Kaleena Smith #11 of Ontario Christian High School poses for a portrait at The Knights Center on November 9, 2026 in Ontario, California. Ric Tapia - The Sporting Tribune Kaleena Smith #11 of Ontario Christian High School poses for a portrait at The Knights Center on November 9, 2026 in Ontario, California. Ontario Christian immediately won the tip off and Kaleena "Special K" Smith sat waiting for a pass at the wing. Without any hesitation, "Special K" puts up a three to make a special shot, to start off senior season with a special moment. "Obviously it is a blessing, but just being able to go out there with a free mind and knowing that if it goes in, it goes in. Really just going out there with a mindset to win. item.title: Iowa Hawkeyes hand Xavier its 1st loss of the season
item.description: Xavier had the opportunity Friday, Nov. 20 to turn an undefeated start into a meaningful early-season statement. Instead, the Musketeers left Cintas Center with a reminder of how quickly an encouraging November can become complicated. With a white out crowd bringing the kind of energy that makes Xavier’s home court one of the most difficult environments in college basketball, the Musketeers couldn’t get past Iowa , falling 83-65 for its first loss of the season while missing an important opportunity to add another high-major victory to their NCAA Tournament resume. Xavier had survived a scare against Cleveland State earlier in the week, with head coach Richard Pitino acknowledging afterward that his team had fallen into a trap with more difficult matchups on the horizon. If the Musketeers were already looking ahead to Iowa, they didn’t get the result they wanted when the more significant test finally arrived. One game after Xavier's defense took a "major step back," the Muskies weren't much better in defending Iowa. The Hawkeyes entered the night shooting 33% from 3-point range this season but soared past that average, going 9-for-13 in the first half to take a 39-32 lead into the locker room. Iowa would stretch its lead to as many as 21 in the second half as Xavier lacked any answer on the defensive end. The Hawkeyes shot over 65% in the second half and finished 14-for-22 from 3-point range behind guard Isaia Howard, who led all scorers with 24 points on 9 of 12 shooting. Mike Nwoko provided a spark early, scoring Xavier's first 11 points, but the Musketeers shot under 35% overall on a night where Iowa made everything difficult for the hosts. Nwoko led Xavier with 21 points, hitting four 3-pointers. He was joined in double figures by Jovan Milicevic (11) and Chance Westry (11). Xavier (5-1) will now have to regroup with two significant opportunities coming up next week against Texas A&M and No. 4 Virginia in the Battle 4 Atlantis in Nassau, Bahamas. item.title: ‘Makes a Mockery of His Legacy’ — NFL Insider Takes Shot at Nicolas Cage-Led John Madden Biopic, Calls It ‘The Biggest Disgrace’
item.description: ‘Makes a Mockery of His Legacy’ — NFL Insider Takes Shot at Nicolas Cage-Led John Madden Biopic, Calls It ‘The Biggest Disgrace’ Iconic NFL coach and commentator John Madden’s biopic, “Madden,” began streaming Nov. 18 to a mixed audience response and largely negative reviews from critics. Oscar-winning actor Nicolas Cage plays Madden in the film, which covers his coaching career with the Oakland Raiders (now the Las Vegas Raiders), his broadcasting work, and his role in the Madden NFL video game franchise. Among the critics is NFL insider Jordan Schultz, who watched the film and did not hold back in a lengthy post on X on Friday. NFL Insider Jordan Schultz Rips John Madden Biopic Schultz called the movie one of the worst sports films he has seen, saying the divisive biopic’s script is “overwritten, unfunny and downright uninspiring.” “I want to preface this by saying I love sports movies… But the new Madden movie might be the biggest disgrace I’ve ever seen. The script is overwritten, unfunny and downright uninspiring. John Madden was an amazing, larger-than-life presence,” Schultz wrote . “The film makes a mockery of his legacy by trying too hard for cheap laughs and repeatedly relying on uninspired humor. I’ll probably need to rewatch it at some point, but I couldn’t have been more disappointed after the first viewing.” Madden is best known as the Raiders’ head coach from 1969 to 1978. He led the franchise to seven division titles, seven AFL/AFC Championship Games, eight playoff appearances, and a win in Super Bowl XI. He never had a losing season and still has the highest winning percentage among head coaches with at least 100 games. After leaving the Raiders, he joined CBS Sports as a color commentator in 1979. He soon teamed with Pat Summerall in the booth, forming one of the most memorable broadcasting duos in league history. Madden became the first person to call games on all four major U.S. TV networks and won 16 Sports Emmy Awards. His final game was Super Bowl XLIII between the Pittsburgh Steelers and Arizona Cardinals on Feb. 1, 2009. Cage, who gained 25 pounds for the role, told People that he knew very little about Madden before taking the part and did not follow football. item.description: Photo by: Randy Sartin Volunteers Overcome Slow Start No. 14 Tennessee continued its impressive start to the basketball season Friday night, taking care of Coastal Carolina with a convincing 78-51 victory at Food City Center. The Volunteers improved to 5-0 on the season, avoiding a letdown after their major win over No. 2 Michigan State earlier in the week. Tennessee did not have its best start, as Coastal Carolina came out aggressive and quickly put pressure on the Volunteers. The Chanticleers knocked down several early three pointers and jumped out to a 9-3 advantage. The Vols struggled to find their rhythm offensively during the opening minutes. However, they eventually began attacking the paint, using their size and physicality to get back into the contest. DeWayne Brown II helped spark the comeback, scoring inside and giving Tennessee a much-needed presence near the basket. Juke Harris also provided an important boost with his energy and ability to create scoring opportunities. Tennessee Takes Control Before Halftime Coastal Carolina continued to make shots early in the first half and remained competitive for much of the opening period. However, Tennessee’s defense eventually began making things difficult for the Chanticleers. The Volunteers closed the half with a strong scoring run, turning a competitive game into a more comfortable advantage. Tennessee entered the locker room with a 41-29 lead after limiting Coastal Carolina’s opportunities during the final stretch. Brown was already making a major impact, reaching double figures before halftime while controlling the boards. The Volunteers opened the second half with an 11-2 run, pushing the lead to 21 points and putting the game out of reach. item.description: Usman Nurmagomedov Getty Top-ranked MMA lightweight fighter Usman Nurmagomedov shared his first comments following his recent arrest in Abu Dhabi. Nurmagomedov and his cronies cowardly attacked UFC bantamweight Merab Dvalishvili and a friend last week at an RAF event in Abu Dhabi in an assault that was captured on video and circulated on social media. Abu Dhabi authorities sentenced eight men to six months in jail, but following an appeal, they were released from prison. Now, Nurmagomedov has spoken out. Usman Nurmagomedov Breaks His Silence Taking to his social media on Friday, Nurmagomedov broke his silence after his arrest in Abu Dhabi and his release from prison, sharing a quote from Marcus Aurelius. “The moment you are offended or praised, you are still a slave.” – Marcus Aurelius View this post on Instagram Brendan Schaub Rips Usman Nurmagomedov After seeing Nurmagomedov’s social media message, former UFC heavyweight fighter Brendan Schaub spoke about it on his podcast, ripping Nurmagomedov to shreds for his lack of accountability. “This is his problem: They’re taking no accountability. They still think it’s okay what they did. (Expletive) him. (Expletive) him. He’s going to get annihilated for that,” Schaub said (via MMAFighting.com ). Nurmagomedov is still a free agent and will be able to speak to the UFC very soon about signing a contract with the world’s leading MMA promotion. As ugly as the incident with Dvalishvili was in Abu Dhabi, it did elevate Nurmagomedov’s profile with UFC fans who may not have known much about him before, so even though there are plenty of UFC fans who have no interest in signing him after cowardly attacking Dvalishvili, it’s unlikely this incident will change the UFC’s mind about signing him. item.title: Ohio State football starting OL Phillip Daniels ruled out vs Nebraska
item.description: Ohio State football will be without offensive lineman Phillip Daniels against Nebraska on Nov. 20, marking the sixth game this season that the Buckeyes ' starting right tackle will miss. Daniels was downgraded from questionable to out in the availability report released by the Big Ten the day before the Nebraska game. The injuries are unspecified in the availability reports. Against Texas on Sept. 12 , Daniels went down late in the fourth quarter. He missed the four matchups following the 24-23 loss to the Longhorns , returning for the Indiana game on Oct. 17. Daniels returned to the injury list ahead of the Nov. 14 game against Northwestern. Junior Ian Moore replaced Daniels in the 28-19 win over the Wildcats, with senior Austin Siereveld sliding over to Moore's former starting position of left tackle. Ohio State coach Ryan Day said Siereveld will remain at left tackle the rest of the season. Starting left guard Luke Montgomery is expected to be available after missing the Northwestern game with an illness. Wide receiver Brock Boyd has been taken off the availability report after starting the week questionable. item.title: Guardians Make Painful David Fry Roster Decision
item.description: KANSAS CITY, MISSOURI - SEPTEMBER 25: David Fry #6 of the Cleveland Guardians hits a home run during the fifth inning against the Kansas City Royals at Kauffman Stadium on September 25, 2026 in Kansas City, Missouri. (Photo by Jay Biggerstaff/Getty Images) Getty CLEVELAND, OHIO - SEPTEMBER 19: David Fry #8 of the Cleveland Guardians runs out a two-RBI double during the third inning against the Athletics at Progressive Field on September 19, 2026 in Cleveland, Ohio. (Photo by Jason Miller/Getty Images) CLEVELAND, OHIO - JULY 01: David Fry #6 of the Cleveland Guardians celebrates as he rounds the bases on a three-run home run during the second inning against the Texas Rangers at Progressive Field on July 01, 2026 in Cleveland, Ohio. (Photo by Jason Miller/Getty Images) The Cleveland Guardians will always have some great memories with David Fry. His story on the shores of Lake Erie appears to be over, though. Fry isn’t set to be with the Guardians in the 2027 MLB season. An important MLB deadline arrived on Friday at 5 p.m. ET — the non-tender deadline. Any player eligible for arbitration has to be tendered a contract by that point in time, essentially saying that a team intends to move forward with that player. A team can also non-tender a player, basically saying that it doesn’t want to give that player a new deal for 2027. Fry took the bad side of that equation. David Fry Roster Decision Getty CLEVELAND, OHIO – SEPTEMBER 19: David Fry #8 of the Cleveland Guardians runs out a two-RBI double during the third inning against the Athletics at Progressive Field on September 19, 2026 in Cleveland, Ohio. (Photo by Jason Miller/Getty Images) The Guardians chose to non-tender Fry, according to multiple reports on Friday night. He was the only player that Cleveland non-tendered. This makes Fry officially a free agent. He can sign with any team. The lockout looms at the start of December, so it’s not clear whether Fry will get a new deal before then or if he’ll have to wait out the lockout and then pursue a new contract. Why Guardians Parted With David Fry Getty CLEVELAND, OHIO – JULY 01: David Fry #6 of the Cleveland Guardians celebrates as he rounds the bases on a three-run home run during the second inning against the Texas Rangers at Progressive Field on July 01, 2026 in Cleveland, Ohio. (Photo by Jason Miller/Getty Images) The painful reality is that Fry had fallen off in a major way from the player he once was. In the 2024 season, he was an All-Star and finished the year hitting .263 with an .804 OPS that included 18 doubles and 14 home runs in 122 games. Fry then hit .171 (.592) OPS in 66 games in 2025 and .201 (.677 OPS) in 91 games in 2026. He still was relied upon by Cleveland to hit lefties, but his overall work at the plate didn’t warrant frequent enough playing time to justify keeping him on the roster now. A serious injury to his throwing elbow severely limited what used to be a lot of versatility provided by Fry, including an ability to catch.

Coming off of a sweep of UMass, the 4-5-2 Eagles looked to continue their momentum after a rough start to the season. Maine, meanwhile, also wanted to recapture some energy after getting swept by BU, splitting with UMass, and tying Vermont. The Maine crowd was energized to start the game and started their chants of “Daddy’s Money” and “BU Rejects” very early, even if they made little sense. BC got the first break of the game when Maine’s Tanner Kilmpke was called for tripping. But the powerplay was largely ineffective and the game continued on its messy, defensive style. Neither team could get much going because of the structured defense and chaotic passing that resulted in several early turnovers. Eventually Maine got a powerplay of their own after the midway point of the first period when Jake Sondreal was called for tripping. But the Black Bears couldn’t convert either. It was a slog until finally Matias Vanhanen passed to Teddy Stiga who broke free in front of Maine goalie Albin Boija and slid one by to give Boston College a 1-0 lead with just a few minutes remaining in the first period. Then BC went on another powerplay when Black Bear Dante Siciliano was called for tripping just before the break. With a 2-0 lead in Orono, the Eagles were in a great position away from home to start the next portion of the contest. BC’s Casey Mutryn was called for holding soon after that as the refs tried to keep the game even, but the Eagles penalty kill again succeeded against the Maine offense. item.description: Mandatory Credit: Gary A. Vasquez-Imagn Images At 13-3, the Los Angeles Lakers have every reason to feel confident going into their latest showdown . At home, against a 1-13 Kings team, every expectation is that the Purple and Gold will come out victorious, regardless of who is available. That’s why, despite making progress in his return from a right heel injury, veteran guard Austin Reaves was ruled out for tonight’s contest. According to one NBA insider, the Lakers have opted to give Reaves some extra time to rest before making his return. Apparently, Luka Doncic (who has experience with heel injuries) spoke to Reaves himself and encouraged him to take as much time as he needed. “Austin Reaves will miss his fourth straight game tonight with that left heel bruise,” reported ESPN’s Dave McMenamin . “This has been improving day by day, I’m told, and it was good news on Wednesday when Reaves was able to get back on the court for a workout. Whether today was a go or not, they want to be cautious on this, cause they recognize he can get three more days of rest leading into their next game on Monday.” “A source close to Luka Doncic told me that he has told Austin personally, ‘I’ve dealt with a bruised heel back in 2024, and it led to a calf strain, which ultimately led to me being traded from the Dallas Mavericks to the Lakers,” McMenamin added . “We don’t want you to be in a similar situation. We’re trying to be in this for the long haul. Take your time now — we’re 13-3, and we’ll hold down the fort.” Lower leg injuries can be tricky, in that one can often lead into another. Luka found this out firsthand during his stint with the Dallas Mavericks years ago, which ultimately led to the calf strain that spelled the end of his time in Dallas. Had Luka taken more time to rest his body back then, things might be very different than they are today. Ultimately, it’s too late for Doncic to take back that decision, but he can use what he learned to help his current teammate avoid making the same mistake. Reaves, 28, hasn’t played since November 11th against the Bucks, when he dropped 18 points, three rebounds, five assists, and three steals in 25 minutes. His recovery has been steady , and it sounds like he was thinking about returning tonight before Luka changed his mind. Opting for the careful approach, Reaves has decided to push back his return until Monday, against the Utah Jazz. Not only does it give Austin a few extra days of recovery, but it ensures that he can get his rhythm in a relatively low-stakes game against a Western Conference bottom-feeder. In the meantime, the Lakers will have to go one more game without him. Against the lowly Kings, it shouldn’t be too hard to pull off a win, but they’ve lost these kinds of games before. item.title: Blue Jays opt not to tender Davis Schneider
item.description: Mandatory Credit: Daniel Kucin Jr.-Imagn Images Blue Jays opt not to tender Davis Schneider appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . In 2025, Toronto Blue Jays left fielder Davis Schneider had a standout World Series performance . One year later, Schneider was in a slump . On Friday, the Blue Jays decided not to tender Schneider, officially releasing him , per Bob Nightengale of USA Today. Under MLB rules, not tendering a contract means that a team declines to offer a contract to a player for the next season who has played fewer than six years. Schneider played four seasons for the Blue Jays. Altogether, Schneider played in 69 games and posted a .145 batting average with 18 hits, 16 RBIs, and five home runs. He began the season with a .250 batting average, hitting a home run and driving in five runs in his first 24 at-bats. Afterward, he went hitless in 14 straight games, and in May, he went 4-for-23. From there, it started to go down. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Over the season, Schneider was sent down to Triple-A Buffalo four times. As his stats dwindled, the Blue Jays endured a struggling season and finished 79-83, last place in the American League East Division. A far cry from the year prior, when they made it to the World Series and took the Los Angeles Dodgers to the brink. During that run, Schneider finished the season with a .234 batting average, 44 hits, 11 home runs, and 31 RBIs. Altogether, Schneider finished the World Series batting .200 with two hits, one home run, one RBI, and one run scored. He led off Game 5 with a first-pitch home run off Dodgers pitcher Blake Snell. Now, Schneider is a free agent. He can sign with any team. item.title: How Columbus Crew turned it all around to set up MLS playoff showdown vs. Messi
item.description: It wasn’t working. Issa Tall had to admit that. Well, he didn’t really have to. The results told the story for him. The Columbus Crew didn’t win in its first five MLS matches. By the World Cup break, 15 games in, they’d only added two more. There needed to be changes, and they needed to be big. The Crew general manager moved quickly. In May, he fired coach Henrik Rydström, his first coaching hire as the Crew’s chief soccer officer, though he was quick to point out he was involved with previous hires including bringing in Wilfried Nancy. He spent big in the summer, revamping the Crew’s attack and adding pieces while bidding farewell to some regulars. Ten players arrived, and eight went out. It worked. The Crew turned the boat around, going from worst in the Eastern Conference to closing the season on a six-game win streak and having won eight of their last nine. That was enough not only to jump out of Thursday’s wild card match but to set up a First Round playoff series with Inter Miami, the reigning champion led by Lionel Messi. They also pushed to the U.S. Open Cup final, falling to St. Louis City in a penalty shootout. All of it led Tall to believe he made the right decisions, moving on quickly from the coach he thought was the right man for the job. “Some people could’ve waited the full year. Maybe it would’ve been safer, but that’s not me. That’s not us as a club. That’s not even the way we play!” Tall told USA TODAY Sports ahead of the playoffs. “You see how we are bold and are not afraid of taking risk. At the end of the day, it wasn’t even a risk necessarily. It was necessary for our players, for our club as a whole and I think ultimately we made the right decision to do it at that time.” Tall still stands by Rydström as a good coach, something he’s proving while leading Hammarby in Sweden which currently sits atop of the table after running off five consecutive wins. But he wasn’t the right fit for the Crew in the post-Nancy era. The Crew turned to Courtois, a former Crew academy and MLS Next Pro coach who continued the idea first expressed on the field so successfully by Nancy’s teams. The squad might not have been the entirely right squad, either. Tall turned to a scouting network led by Mark Nichols, bringing in a proven MLS veteran in Santi Rodriguez, Chile national team forward Gonzalo Tapia, securing a loan deal for Moroccan winger Anass Zaroury and signing designated player Brais Mendez, a Spanish attacker whose arrival from Real Sociedad brought to mind that of Cucho Hernandez. item.title: Gotham FC’s title defense comes to crushing end in semifinal loss after venue change
item.description: They came by car, by the special-event X80 bus, by bike if they were feeling sporty. They came in layers, in beanies and scarves, with Gotham’s black-and-sky-blue colors on top. They came on behalf of those who couldn’t come, capacity being reduced at this impromptu change of venue, each one trying to make noise for five. IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect They came with some measure of outrage — these home-field shenanigans would never happen in men’s sports — while their better angels told them to come in joy, in celebration, everyone watching women’s sports. And then, 25 miles and 20,000 seats removed from their regular destination at New Jersey’s Sports Illustrated Stadium, huddled in the bleachers by a blue track ringing an immaculate pitch at Icahn Stadium on Randall’s Island, in the shadow of the old Psychiatric Center and with the light fading over the Costco across the river, 5,000 devoted souls Sunday afternoon watched Gotham’s NWSL title defense end in a 2-1 semifinal loss to the Kansas City Current. “We lost today because we weren’t the better team,” Gotham winger and oracle Midge Purce said. “That being said, I would say it’s inexcusable. It’s not what you want in a professional league. It’s not what you want for women who are progressing in the United States and supposed to be one of the best leagues in the entire world. I think it’s a bad look for everyone involved. And we always want to be at Sports Illustrated in front of our fans when we earned that right throughout the season. But I would say it had no effect on performance today.” The match had been moved to Icahn on Monday due to concerns over the disintegrating field conditions at Sports Illustrated, which had unfortunately overshadowed Gotham’s quarterfinal victory there last weekend. Gotham was unbeaten in its past 13 matches at Sports Illustrated, which is operated by the Red Bulls of MLS. item.title: Beckham to be inducted into US Soccer Hall of Fame
item.description: David Beckham was knighted by King Charles in 2025 [Getty Images] David Beckham will be inducted into the United States' National Soccer Hall of Fame as part of its 2027 class. The former Manchester United and England midfielder, 51, made headlines in 2007 when he moved to Los Angeles from Spanish giants Real Madrid to join Major League Soccer (MLS) side LA Galaxy on a five-year contract. He made 124 appearances in all competitions for Galaxy, scoring 20 goals, and twice won both the MLS Cup and Supporters' Shield. Beckham's six seasons at Galaxy helped to raise the global profile of MLS and following his retirement in 2013, he became co-owner of MLS club Inter Miami, who signed Argentina World Cup winner Lionel Messi in 2023. His induction ceremony is set to take place on 16 April 2027 in Frisco, Texas. David Beckham's deal with LA Galaxy in 2007 was reportedly worth £128m [Getty Images] He was told the news he had been chosen on the veterans' ballot at an MLS board of governors' meeting on Thursday and said his time in the US has been "an incredible journey". Beckham, who had two loan spells with AC Milan in 2009 and 2010 while at Galaxy, added: "I'm looking to build this league and this sport in this great country for a long time." Meanwhile, former US internationals Megan Rapinoe and Julie Ertz have also been voted into the Hall of Fame in their first year of eligibility. Ballon d'Or winner Rapinoe, 41, and midfielder Ertz, 34, lifted the Women’s World Cup twice with with the US in 2015 and 2019. "To be alongside all the greatest players that have played for us, and played for our country alongside a bunch of my team-mates and friends, recognised like that in this way just means you were successful and a part of great teams," Rapinoe wrote on Instagram. item.title: Messi makes history with MLS Golden Boot
item.description: Messi retired from international football with Argentina earlier this year [Getty Images] Inter Miami forward Lionel Messi has become the first player in MLS history to win the Golden Boot in consecutive seasons. The eight-time Ballon d'Or winner scored 26 goals in 31 appearances, four clear of FC Dallas striker Peter Musa and five more than Nashville's English forward Sam Surridge. Messi becomes only the sixth player to land the award twice, joining a list that includes former Charlton Athletic and Southampton striker Bradley Wright-Phillips. In addition to his goals, the 39-year-old notched 17 assists over the course of the MLS season, ensuring his 43 goal contributions was also a league best for the second year in a row. And the World Cup winner could soon make more history as he bids to become the first three-time Landon Donovan MLS MVP winner. The former Argentina forward landed the award in 2024 as Inter Miami won the Supporters' Shield title and also in 2025 as they won the MLS Cup. Despite Messi's magic, Miami weren't able to land top spot in the MLS Eastern Conference, with the team finishing 17 points behind Surridge's Nashville. They will now face Columbus Crew over three games in the first round of the MLS Cup play-offs which begin later this month. item.title: On MLS Decision Day, D.C. United faces a familiar reality: Another season of failure
item.description: WASHINGTON — All around Major League Soccer , from Montreal to Miami and Seattle to San Diego, Saturday was Decision Day — the last act in an 8½-month production. While three playoff berths were in the balance, teams with guaranteed spots sought to improve their place. It's a day marked by desperation, scoreboard-watching and playoff-planning. At Audi Field, however, Decision Day felt more like Derision Day. For the seventh consecutive year, D.C. United, once a showpiece of a blossoming league, has no playoff plans — a near impossibility in a league that distributes postseason passes like a guy on a New York street corner handing out flyers for discount mattresses. Only Toronto FC's eight-year rut, starting with its 2007 expansion campaign, lasted longer. United wasn't even in the mix on Decision Day, its fate having been decided 10 days earlier. The lowly finale was against another failed side, New York City FC, which claimed a 1-0 victory on a late goal. While 2026 was an anomaly for the New Yorkers, it was the norm in the nation's capital. D.C. added another sad chapter to a rotten story under an ownership group, led by Jason Levien and Steve Kaplan, that has dragged the organization into irrelevance in not just the prospering league but in the local market and the ascending sport. The public-address announcer introduces the team as "your four-time MLS Cup champions," but he's been saying that for a long time. Given the league's evolution, it feels even longer. United's last title, in 2004, came in a 10-team operation — one-third the current landscape. Since then, 13 different clubs have hoisted the trophy. Less than two miles north of Audi Field, the U.S. Capitol witnessed a historic sea change Tuesday with a political wave that swept the ruling party out of office. Local soccer fans have had no such luck with those in power at Audi Field. Under the current regime … United hasn't won a playoff game in 11 years and hasn't advanced to the conference finals in 14. Twelve years have passed since it won at least half its 34 matches. United's only trophy in recent memory was the 2013 U.S. Open Cup, which came amid a horrific, three-win regular season. D.C. is on its fourth head coach since Ben Olsen's departure in late 2020 and its second head of soccer operations in four years. The current director, Erkut Sogut — an agent best known for representing former German star Mesut Özil — was hired last fall without any experience working for a team. Another goal conceded, another season to forget. Keisuke Kurokawa's frustration summed up D.C. United's latest disappointing chapter.
